Jeshurun
JESH-u-run
n. (proper, a poetic name of Israel; Hebrew, the upright one)
Hebrew Yeshuruwn, a diminutive of endearment from yashar, upright — little upright one. It occurs three times in the songs of Moses and once in Isaiah, and it is the name God uses for Israel when he is speaking most tenderly and most severely.

Biblical Definition

The name is used first in an indictment, and the tenderness in it makes the charge worse: “But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked: thou art waxen fat, thou art grown thick, thou art covered with fatness; then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation” (Deuteronomy 32:15). The upright one grew fat on God's own bounty and used the strength to kick. Then the blessing: “And he was king in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people and the tribes of Israel were gathered together” (Deuteronomy 33:5) — God himself reigning over the assembly. And the last verse of that blessing: “There is none like unto the God of Jeshurun, who rideth upon the heaven in thy help, and in his excellency on the sky” (Deuteronomy 33:26). Isaiah uses it once more, promising the Spirit poured upon the seed. God calls his people upright not because they are, but because he has determined they shall be.

Origin & Era

Webster (1828) has no entry for this proper name; Scripture fixes it as a poetical and endearing title of Israel, signifying the upright one.

expand to see more

UPRIGHT, a. Erect; perpendicular; and figuratively, honest; just; adhering to rectitude in all social intercourse.

ENDEARMENT, n. The act of endearing, or state of being endeared; that which excites or increases affection.

KICK, v.i. To strike with the foot; and figuratively, to spurn; to reject with scorn or contumely.

PROSPERITY, n. Advance or gain in anything good or desirable; successful progress in any business or enterprise.

ROCK, n. In Scripture, a figure of God as a defence, a refuge, and the firm foundation of his people.

Key Scripture

Deuteronomy 32:15 — "But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked: thou art waxen fat, thou art grown thick, thou art covered with fatness; then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation."

Deuteronomy 33:5 — "And he was king in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people and the tribes of Israel were gathered together."

Deuteronomy 33:26 — "There is none like unto the God of Jeshurun, who rideth upon the heaven in thy help, and in his excellency on the sky."

Isaiah 44:2 — "Thus saith the LORD that made thee, and formed thee from the womb, which will help thee; Fear not, O Jacob, my servant; and thou, Jesurun, whom I have chosen."

Modern Corruption

Prosperity is sought as a sign of God's favour and treated as spiritually neutral, where Deuteronomy 32 names abundance as the very thing that made Jeshurun kick and forsake the God who made him.

expand to see more

Deuteronomy 32:15 is the Bible's classic account of what plenty does to a people, and the verbs are brutal: waxed fat, and kicked. The picture is a well-fed animal turning on the hand that fed it. Three clauses pile up the abundance — waxen fat, grown thick, covered with fatness — and then two clauses state the result: he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation. Nothing had gone wrong with the circumstances. The circumstances were the danger, and Moses had warned about it two chapters earlier: when thou hast eaten and art full, beware lest thou forget the LORD.

The other uses guard against reading this as gloom about God's goodness. He is king in Jeshurun when the heads of the people are gathered; there is none like unto the God of Jeshurun, who rideth upon the heaven in thy help. The problem is never the gift; it is the receiver's forgetting. And the name itself is grace: God calls a people who kicked him the upright one, a diminutive of affection, because he sees them as what his covenant will make them. Isaiah uses it while promising to pour water on him that is thirsty and his Spirit upon their seed.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Yeshuruwn (H3484), the upright one; yashar (H3477), straight, upright; shamen (H8080), to grow fat; tsuwr (H6697), a rock.

expand to see more

Hebrew Yeshuruwn (H3484) — Jeshurun; a diminutive of endearment, the upright little one.

Hebrew yashar (H3477) — straight, right, upright; the root of the name.

Hebrew shamen (H8080) — to grow fat, to be sleek; Jeshurun waxed fat and kicked.

Hebrew nabal (H5034) — to be foolish, to esteem lightly; he lightly esteemed the Rock.

Hebrew tsuwr (H6697) — a rock, a cliff; the Rock of his salvation.

Usage

"“But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked” — what abundance did."

"“And he was king in Jeshurun” — God reigning over the assembly."

"“There is none like unto the God of Jeshurun” — the last word of the blessing."
